correctness.rationale: Normalize the centers to 0,D; this preserves the positive weight magnitudes. For a scalar rank-two compression, the min–max principle already gives Re(e^{-iθ}z) ≤ λ₂(Hθ). With u=D cos θ, the four eigenvalues are ±r and u±s. For |u|≤r+s the second is min(r,u+s), so if D≤r+s the inequalities give precisely the disk intersection as an upper bound. Every point of that intersection is achieved by a pair of unit vectors, one in each block, with the prescribed scalar expectation (the numerical range of a 2×2 Jordan block is the disk). At D>r+s the directions cos θ=±(r+s)/D, each with both sine signs, force Im z=0 and Re z=Dr/(r+s). An isometry with block components √(s/(r+s)) I and √(r/(r+s)) diag(1,−1) attains it by exact off-diagonal cancellation. This establishes the formula even without sufficiency of the general half-plane characterization. Coincident centers, containment/tangency and external tangency follow directly; the normal limit is the whole segment since weighted block copies of the identity realize every point and ordinary expectations bound the range by the segment. Eventually the separated formula applies along every stated vanishing-weight path; all ratios, including both endpoints, can occur in the limit.
residual_risks: The rational checks are supplementary; the continuum range and all path limits are established analytically.
